  > 
  > Where they do not carry the Brief:
  > - **P5 / C6: not supported** under the Brief's rule (pooled held-out gain 0.034 [−0.285, 0.338]; positive in 3 of 6 mechanisms; bias part 0.008; within-cell excess 0.0007). Part (i) on D* is met (gain 0.125 [0.069, 0.318]). The exact-theory predictor explains the bias in 82% of cells, so the account holds; no data-computable score does.
  > - **P2: bias independent of d is false for (b)** (median |bias| 0.115 → 0.025 → 0.007 for d=5,20,80) **and for (d)** (0.17 → 0.48 → 0.45); it holds for (c), (e), (f).
  > - **P1 (variance):** the d exponent is 0.55 [0.547, 0.556], not ½, at all three σ.
  > - **Inference:** mean coverage of the HC0 interval is 0.745 (nominal 0.95); it tracks |bias|/SD, not leverage (coverage by L quartile at |bias|/SD<0.25: 0.93/0.95/0.93/0.90). The leverage prediction for coverage is not what shows.
  > - **C7:** the synthetic threshold-mechanism failure (regression loses at d=20) does not transfer to Stanford3 or ego-Facebook (regression wins at all d).
  > 
  > What I will write unless you object: thesis = variance predictable from leverage; bias predictable only with the mechanism (not from one experiment's data); regression beats DM above a break-even spillover share that grows with d; the standard interval undercovers because of bias. Headline pair = regime map + mechanism-specific bias; C6 and C8 are reported negatives in the main text; contribution type stays General.
  > 
  > Asks: (1) confirm or change that thesis; the Brief says a failed P5 turns the claim into which feature does predict error, and I read that as the exact-theory predictor plus the estimation-noise diagnosis I asked `analysis` for. (2) Update P1 (d exponent), P2 and P5 in the Brief to what was found, so `report` has one source. (3) Say whether the threshold-mechanism result on real graphs needs a follow-up cell set or is stated as a scope limit.
